title: RWB-S9-E6030-APP: the panel slice owns no fee-schedule, service-level or version storage, publishes no write operation, and its feature has no requirement row
source: Template and Rules v1 R3, R5.4, R5.5, R7.2, R7.3 and R9; context pack S9 rwb-partner; split plan story line RWB-S9-E6030-APP; FSD S9 Partner management v3 A1.2, A1.3, A1.4, A2.2 and Screens; TSD S9 Partner management v2 T2, T3.0, T3.1, T3.2, T5.2, T5.3, T6.1, T6.2, T8 and T-A.1; legacy RWB-E6-030; the thin-story extract Recovery Workbench Business Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3.md
section: Metadata (Depends on (build), Contract dependencies); Sections 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12.1 to 12.5, 14, 16 and 18
description: (1) The feature keeps the panel, the fee schedule and the service level as versioned reference data, but the Ownership Map gives S9 three tables only (partner, partner_instruction, partner_user) and no fee-schedule and no service-level table, while the default ruling of R3 puts parameters and reference data with P3 rwb-case. (2) The six operations of the Ownership Map are two reads and four partner-portal writes, and none maintains the panel, the fee schedule or the service level, so the FSD primary role holds a maintenance screen that no operation serves. (3) The versioned-data semantics have no storage: DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007 and DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016 carry no version column, so the version in force can be stamped on the answer and the decision record but an instruction cannot pin the version it was issued under. (4) The field catalogue of FSD S9 A2.2.3.2 lists partner and partner_instruction fields only and TSD S9 T3.1 has no field catalogue for partner_user, so one of the three owned tables has no shape. (5) No requirement row maps to FEAT-PRM-02: TSD S9 T8 maps REQ-S9-001 to REQ-S9-004 to FEAT-PRM-01 and REQ-S9-005 to REQ-S9-007 and REQ-S9-009 to FEAT-PRM-08, so the requirement column of the fragment is empty. (6) The FSD primary role Reference data administrator is not a role of TSD S9 T6.1, which lists 23 bank roles and six partner roles, and the legacy permission row names eight roles and says 'and 21 more'. (7) The Ownership Map gives two events as EV-20 and EV-21 with no names while TSD S9 T5.3 names InstructionIssued and PartnerResultSubmitted; neither is a panel event, so this key publishes none and the pattern set's DP-09 and DP-14 are applied in no row. (8) The split plan gives this slice AC2 only, so AC1 has no criterion here and legacy TC-E6-030-01 is carried without the criterion it covers. (9) The thin-story extract of the business specification for Epics 3 to 8 is not present in _work/msr/extract, so fill-order step 4 of R7.3 could not be read and every business value comes from the legacy story, FSD S9 and TSD S9.
evidence: Context pack S9 ownership rows (Tables 3: partner, partner_instruction, partner_user; REST 6: two GET and four POST; Events EV-20 and EV-21; Jobs 0; Workflows 1) and naming rules; FSD S9 A2.2.1 to A2.2.4, A1.3, A1.4 and the Screens table; TSD S9 T3.1 (DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-016), T3.2 (LOV-PANEL, LOV-PARTNER-TYPE), T5.2, T5.3, T6.1, T8 and T-A.1 with T-A.2; legacy RWB-E6-030 data table naming timer, partner, decision_log_entry, rule_row and lov_value; Template and Rules v1 R3 default ruling and R5.5 DP-03, DP-07, DP-09, DP-13, DP-14 and DP-19 rows; story line RWB-S9-E6030-APP with four H rows and one C row
area: Ownership, data model, dependency and trace
legacy_ref: RWB-E6-030 (sections Story, Data, Endpoints, Permission checks and Test cases)
proposed: Keep the plan's H and C rows as they stand; hold the panel in partner with the four LOV-PANEL values and the eight LOV-PARTNER-TYPE values read from rwb-case at the version in force; declare no fee-schedule and no service-level table and read both as reference data; build the two published reads and the panel version load behind the same guard, and raise the missing maintenance operation, the missing version column and the missing partner_user catalogue to P3 and P4 for the next contract revision.

title: RWB-S9-E6030-CON: the panel baseline has no published write operation, no path for the reference-data read, no status-to-message mapping and no level on the legacy cases
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.2 and R9; context pack S9 rwb-partner; split plan story line RWB-S9-E6030-CON; TSD S9 Partner management v2 T3.1, T3.2, T6.1, T6.2, T8 and T-A.1 with T-A.2; FSD S9 Partner management v3 A2.2.3.2 and Screens; legacy RWB-E6-030
section: Metadata (Depends on (build), Contract dependencies); Sections 3, 5, 7, 11, 12.1 to 12.8, 14 and 16
description: (1) The baseline is a contract for holding the panel as versioned data, and no write operation for the panel, the fee schedule or the service level is published in the Ownership Map, so section 12.1 declares two reads and an explicit absence instead of a maintenance surface. (2) The reference-data read of rwb-case has no published path or operation name in the S9 sources and the plan's C row sits on the app slice, so the row is declared against RWB-P3-E1043-CON with a placeholder and faked. (3) TSD S9 T-A.2 gives error sets as status codes only, with no message id per condition, so each status is bound to a legacy or FSD message. (4) The legacy test cases of RWB-E6-030 carry no level, so each is mapped to Contract here and to Component on the app slice. (5) partner_user has no field catalogue in TSD S9 T3.1, so the baseline declares the table as owned and no element for it. (6) The fee schedule and the service levels have no element and no owned table to declare, so the baseline declares the reference-data stamp instead of a schedule element. (7) The two event ids EV-20 and EV-21 have no published pairing with the two names of TSD S9 T5.3 and neither is a panel event, so the baseline declares no event and records the pairing for the instruction keys.
evidence: Context pack S9 ownership rows (Tables 3, REST 6, Events EV-20 and EV-21, Jobs 0, Workflows 1); TSD S9 T-A.1 API-S9-001 and API-S9-003 and T-A.2 error lists 401, 403, 503 without message ids; TSD S9 T3.1 and T3.2; FSD S9 A2.2.3.2 field catalogue and Screens; legacy RWB-E6-030 Test cases and Validation and messages; Template and Rules v1 R5.7.1 (a CON story has no build dependency) and R7.2 s16
legacy_ref: RWB-E6-030 (sections Endpoints, Validation and messages, Test cases)
proposed: Publish the fragment as a tagged addendum to the service contract baseline of rwb-partner with the two reads, the Partner element, the two lists, the version stamp, the consumed reference-data row and the decision element; publish no write operation and record the absence; bind each status to a message of section 14; and raise the version column, the partner_user catalogue and the maintenance operation to the next contract revision.
